full_judgment: 18. We now turn to merits of the case. The High Court set aside the decision of the executing Court on two grounds : First is that the decree itself was fraudulent being against a fictitious person namely Niher Bala Whereas the actual tenant was Uttama, Devi; Second ground is that the executing court was in error in holding that there Was no proof of any agreement of purchase first between Uttama and Azim and thereafter between Azim and Respondent Obaidul, Huq and in any event they as prospective purchasers were not representative of the judgment debtor. On the reversal of the finding of identity it is to be remembered, that the executing court has held that Niher Bala and Uttama Devi were the same person and though there was some misdescription, the judgment-debtor was identifiable. Whether the judgment-debtor is or is not identifiable is within the jurisdiction of executing court to decide. It has so decided on some evidence. The High Court in revision, however, profoundly it differed from the conclusion and the appreciation of evidence of the executing court, it could not interfere with the conclusion of the subordinate court as the supposed error does not affect its exercise of jurisdiction in any way.
